summary: Extend the built multiquadratic and narrow genus theory by an explicit real quadratic kernel statement, descent of real class characters, exact cardinalities of genus fibres, and the arithmetic sign criteria used in real quadratic period formulas. Compare the imported form character with the existing ideal character at positive fundamental discriminants, keeping general form carriers and character well-definedness with Geometry of Numbers.

nodes.title: The exact real narrow defect
nodes.statement: Under C, for every A∈Cl⁺(K), π(A)=1 iff A=1 or A=J. Thus the kernel, as a set, is {1,J}, allowing the two entries to coincide. The subgroup it generates is ⟨J⟩ and C/⟨J⟩≅Cl(K) by the existing first isomorphism theorem.
hypotheses: K is a number field; θ∈𝓞 K; minpolyℤ(θ)=X²−d and ℚ[θ]=K; d is squarefree and positive; D=fundamentalDiscriminant(d)>1; C=Cl⁺(K), π the forgetful map and J=mkPrincipal(θ).
proofSteps: Use toClassGroup_ker to write every kernel element as mkPrincipal(x).
Apply mkPrincipal_eq_one_or_eq_mkPrincipal_gen. Conversely π kills both one and the principal class J.
Import mkPrincipal_sq, hence J²=1; use quotientKerEquivOfSurjective for the quotient formulation.
acceptance: Do not assert the kernel has two distinct elements when J=1.
A norm−1 integral unit makes the kernel trivial by the imported injectivity criterion.
With no norm−1 unit, the two possible representatives are distinct and every wide fibre is {A,JA}.

sources.match: Exact set form of the quotient by the distinguished principal class.

nodes.title: Descent of an even real class character
nodes.statement: Under C, for every homomorphism χ:C→ℤˣ, there exists exactly one ψ:ClassGroup(𝓞 K)→ℤˣ with ψ∘π=χ iff χ(J)=1.
hypotheses: K is a number field; θ∈𝓞 K; minpolyℤ(θ)=X²−d and ℚ[θ]=K; d is squarefree and positive; D=fundamentalDiscriminant(d)>1; C=Cl⁺(K), π the forgetful map and J=mkPrincipal(θ).
χ is a multiplicative homomorphism; no assertion is made for an arbitrary function.
proofSteps: Use the exact kernel theorem to see χ kills ker π exactly when χ(J)=1.
Apply QuotientGroup.lift and the surjective first-isomorphism equivalence to obtain ψ.
The equation on every π(A) proves uniqueness by surjectivity. The converse evaluates that equation at J.
acceptance: The trivial character descends uniquely.
A character taking −1 on J cannot descend.
If J=1 every real class character descends; if J is a nontrivial square, every genus character descends but arbitrary complex characters need not.

sources.match: The source descent statement with existence and uniqueness made explicit.

nodes.title: The number of classes in each narrow genus
nodes.statement: Under C and the factorization s from F, for every g∈NumberField.NarrowClassGroup.ElementaryTwoQuotient(K), put G_g={A∈C:q(A)=g} using the existing q. Then 2^(|s|−1)·Nat.card(G_g)=Nat.card(C). All fibres are nonempty, finite, and have equal cardinality. Here |s|=ω(D) is the ramified prime count; h⁺=Nat.card(C), never the ordinary class number.
hypotheses: K is a number field; θ∈𝓞 K; minpolyℤ(θ)=X²−d and ℚ[θ]=K; d is squarefree and positive; D=fundamentalDiscriminant(d)>1; C=Cl⁺(K), π the forgetful map and J=mkPrincipal(θ).
Prime-discriminant factorization s as in F; the genus g is arbitrary.
proofSteps: Use elementaryTwoQuotientEquivSquareQuotient to identify the existing additive quotient with the quotient by squares.
For the quotient homomorphism, fiberEquivKerOfSurjective identifies any fibre with the square subgroup. Apply the subgroup cardinality identity.
Replace the quotient cardinality by 2^twoRank and narrowTwoRank_eq_ncard_ramifiedPrimes_sub_one; ncard_ramifiedPrimes_eq_card replaces the ramification count by |s|.
The existing quotient surjectivity and narrow finiteness give nonempty finite fibres. The equation determines their common cardinality since the power of two is positive.
acceptance: For s={5} or s={8}, the only genus contains all narrow classes.
For D=12 or 28, s has two elements and each genus has h⁺/2 classes.
For D=60, s={−4,−3,5}; each of its four genera has h⁺/4 classes.
Replacing C/C² by C[2] is rejected: even for a cyclic group of order 8, a genus fibre has four elements whereas the 2-torsion subgroup has two.

sources.match: Integral form of the displayed cardinality, avoiding a negative natural exponent.

nodes.title: The sign of a composite genus character
nodes.statement: Under C and F, the integer value of χ_t(J) equals sign(δ). Since D=δδ′>0 and δ,δ′ are nonzero, it also equals sign(δ′). For t empty and t=s this value is 1.
hypotheses: K is a number field; θ∈𝓞 K; minpolyℤ(θ)=X²−d and ℚ[θ]=K; d is squarefree and positive; D=fundamentalDiscriminant(d)>1; C=Cl⁺(K), π the forgetful map and J=mkPrincipal(θ).
s is a finite set of prime discriminants, at most one even, with product D; t⊆s; δ=∏t and δ′=∏(s∖t); χ_t is the existing narrow genus character valued in ℤˣ={±1}.
proofSteps: Use genusCharFunNarrowClassGroupHom_eq_prod_singleton. Evaluate each singleton at J by the built genusCharFunNarrowClassGroupHom_mkPrincipal_gen.
The finite product of the nonzero factors’ signs is the sign of their product.
The complementary factors have positive product D, so their signs agree. Import isFundamentalDiscriminant_prod to include both the empty product and genuine complementary discriminants.
acceptance: D=12=(-4)(-3): each singleton character is −1 on J, while the empty and full characters are 1.
D=24=(-8)(-3) uses the negative dyadic factor −8; substituting8 changes the discriminant.
D=8 has the positive dyadic singleton and sign1.
D=136=8·17 has all these values1 even when the narrow defect is nontrivial.
No extension of sign(δ)=sign(δ′) is allowed when D<0.

sources.match: Composite extension of the pinned singleton theorem; positive-discriminant qualification is recorded in sourceIssues.

nodes.title: Positive prime discriminants and prime divisors
nodes.statement: For D>0 and a finite set s of prime discriminants with at most one even member and product D, (∀P∈s,0<P) iff (∀p∈ℕ, p prime and p∣D imply p mod4≠3). The statement includes D=1 with s empty.
hypotheses: D is positive; s consists of distinct prime discriminants; at most one is even; ∏s=D.
proofSteps: An odd prime discriminant is p or −p according as p is 1 or3 modulo4. Each underlying prime divides D. Conversely any prime divisor of D divides one factor and is its underlying prime by natCast_dvd_primeDiscriminant_iff.
If no prime 3 modulo4 divides D, every odd member is positive. The sole possible even member cannot be −4 or −8 because the product of the other members is positive and D>0. Hence it is 8.
In the forward direction all odd members are positive, so their primes are 1 modulo4; the underlying prime of an even member is2. The empty case is vacuous.
acceptance: D=12 and24 fail because3 divides D.
D=5,8,40 and136 pass, including dyadic8.
The positivity hypothesis is essential: D=−4 has no prime 3 modulo4 divisor but its prime discriminant is negative.

sources.match: Arithmetic expansion of the source no-prime3-modulo4 condition using the prime-discriminant conventions.

nodes.title: The two-square criterion for a fundamental discriminant
nodes.statement: For a positive fundamental discriminant D (including 1), (∃x,y∈ℤ,D=x²+y²) iff (∀p∈ℕ,p prime and p∣D imply p mod4≠3).
proofSteps: Apply Nat.eq_sq_add_sq_iff to D.natAbs and convert between integer squares and squares of natural absolute values.
By the defining fundamental-discriminant alternatives, every odd prime dividing D occurs to exponent exactly 1: D itself is squarefree, or D=4e with e squarefree.
A prime 3 modulo4 is odd, so its exponent cannot be even when present. If there is no such prime divisor, the Mathlib valuation condition is vacuous. No condition is imposed on the exponent of 2.
acceptance: D=12 is not a sum of two integer squares.
Dropping fundamentality breaks the no-divisor criterion:9=0²+3² despite the prime divisor3.

sources.match: Specialization of the full Mathlib two-squares theorem to fundamental discriminants.

nodes.title: The distinguished class in the principal genus
nodes.statement: Under C and F, J∈C² iff no prime p≡3 modulo4 divides D, iff D=x²+y² with integer x,y. Equivalently every genus character χ_t has χ_t(J)=1; by RQ.0 every such character then descends uniquely to the wide class group.
hypotheses: K is a number field; θ∈𝓞 K; minpolyℤ(θ)=X²−d and ℚ[θ]=K; d is squarefree and positive; D=fundamentalDiscriminant(d)>1; C=Cl⁺(K), π the forgetful map and J=mkPrincipal(θ).
s is a finite set of prime discriminants, at most one even, with product D; t⊆s; δ=∏t and δ′=∏(s∖t); χ_t is the existing narrow genus character valued in ℤˣ={±1}.
proofSteps: Import isSquare_mkPrincipal_gen_iff; it already proves J square iff every prime discriminant is positive.
Apply primeDiscriminants_positive_iff and fundamental_sumTwoSquares_iff. The factor product is fundamental by isFundamentalDiscriminant_prod.
The built principal genus theorem tests the singleton characters, and the product decomposition tests all subset characters. Character descent uses RQ.0.
acceptance: D=12 has J outside the principal genus; D=136 has J inside it.
The condition is not asserted equivalent to a norm−1 integral unit: that tests J=1, which is stronger.
All genera and all characters are narrow throughout. The condition does not turn the full prime-discriminant compositum into a totally real field.

sources.match: The source principal-genus criterion, with its weaker-versus-trivial-class distinction explicit.

nodes.title: A sufficient obstruction to a trivial narrow defect
nodes.statement: Under C and F, if p is a natural prime, p∣D and p mod4=3, then J≠1. Consequently π is not injective, the kernel has two distinct elements, h⁺(D)=2h(D), and no unit of 𝓞 K has norm−1. The conclusions use the exact kernel and existing norm-unit and cardinality theorems.
hypotheses: K is a number field; θ∈𝓞 K; minpolyℤ(θ)=X²−d and ℚ[θ]=K; d is squarefree and positive; D=fundamentalDiscriminant(d)>1; C=Cl⁺(K), π the forgetful map and J=mkPrincipal(θ).
s is a finite set of prime discriminants, at most one even, with product D; t⊆s; δ=∏t and δ′=∏(s∖t); χ_t is the existing narrow genus character valued in ℤˣ={±1}.
p prime; (p:ℤ) divides D; p modulo4 equals3.
proofSteps: The principal-genus arithmetic theorem implies J is not square. Since 1 is a square, J≠1.
Use the exact pair kernel to see π is not injective; apply the imported norm−1 injectivity equivalence.
The exact kernel has cardinality 2. The existing narrow-class-number/ordinary-class-number/kernel formula gives h⁺=2h.
acceptance: For d=3,D=12, p=3 obstructs J=1.
For d=7,D=28, p=7 gives the same obstruction.

The converse is not part of this theorem; D=136 has no prime 3 modulo4 divisor while the negative Pell equation for34 has no integral solution. This last distinction is a source/library acceptance example, not a new Pell theorem here.

sources.locator: §2, p.951, paragraph before minus continued fractions
sources.match: The routed sufficient-condition item derived through the stronger genus obstruction.

nodes.title: Agreement of fundamental form and ideal characters
nodes.statement: Under C and F, let Q=[a,b,c] be an integral primitive binary form of discriminant D, associated to the narrow class A by the oriented norm-form dictionary of DIT16 §2. Let the supplied GN.2 character be χ_δ. Then χ_δ(Q)=(χ_t(A):ℤ). A declaration can equivalently take the supplier’s concrete positive represented integer m, coprimality with δ, and nonzero integral ideal B in A⁻¹ with absolute norm m as explicit witness arguments; it must not assume the comparison conclusion.
hypotheses: K is a number field; θ∈𝓞 K; minpolyℤ(θ)=X²−d and ℚ[θ]=K; d is squarefree and positive; D=fundamentalDiscriminant(d)>1; C=Cl⁺(K), π the forgetful map and J=mkPrincipal(θ).
s is a finite set of prime discriminants, at most one even, with product D; t⊆s; δ=∏t and δ′=∏(s∖t); χ_t is the existing narrow genus character valued in ℤˣ={±1}.
Q has integer coefficients, gcd(a,b,c)=1, and b²−4ac=D.

Q represents A through IntegralLattices Layer B2, specialized to the maximal order and transported to the existing NarrowClassGroup. In a properly equivalent representative with a>0, use w^σ<w, w=(-b+√D)/(2a), the fractional ideal 𝔞=wℤ+ℤ, and Q(x,y)=N(x−wy)/N(𝔞). For a<0 the supplier’s oriented sign clause is mandatory; do not use the unoriented coefficient ideal alone.

GN.2 supplies the same Kronecker normalization as genusCharFun(t,·). GN.3 supplies only the specialization/convention and positive coprime represented-value/norm-ideal adapters to the already planned IntegralLattices B2–B3 dictionary; it does not rebuild that dictionary.
proofSteps: Consume IntegralLattices B2–B3 and normalize by a proper basis change to a>0. The GN.3 adapter gives m>0 represented by Q and coprime to δ. For α=x−wy in 𝔞, the associated ideal B=(α)𝔞⁻¹ is integral, nonzero, has absolute norm m, and class A⁻¹: N(𝔞)>0 and Q(x,y)>0 give N(α)>0. Transfer back using proper invariance.
Use GN.2 represented-value evaluation to compute χ_δ(Q)=genusCharFun(t,m).
Use genusCharFunNarrowClassGroupHom_mk0 and genusCharFunCoprimeIdealHom_apply to compute χ_t(A⁻¹) by the same arithmetic value.
A homomorphism valued in ℤˣ has χ_t(A⁻¹)=χ_t(A), proving equality. Changes of basis and representative use the supplied invariance laws, not a new form theory.
acceptance: The principal form [1,0,−3], D=12, represents 1 and has each form genus character 1. Its negative represents3 at (0,1); χ_{−4}(−Q)=−1 agrees with χ_{−4}(J).
For [1,1,−1], D=5, the only character (δ=1 or5) is trivial.

The dyadic zero case [2,0,−6], D=48=(−4)(−12), has χ_{−4}=0 because its content shares 2 with δ. D=48 is not fundamental, so it is outside the comparison even though the supplied general form character is defined.
Use [a,−b,c]↔A⁻¹, [−a,b,−c]↔JA, and −Q↔JA⁻¹; the last two have sign factor sign(δ), not an unconditional identical character.

gaps.title: Concrete supplier signatures for the fundamental form comparison
gaps.detail: The pinned libraries and current GN.2/GN.3 packet have no canonical binary genus-character evaluation or positive coprime norm-witness adapter with these signatures. Current IntegralLattices Layer B2–B3 already plans the oriented form/ideal dictionary into GlobalNumberFields NarrowPic; consume it, specialize at a positive fundamental discriminant, and identify its maximal-order target with the pinned NarrowClassGroup. Match DIT16 §2 p.952: after a proper change to a>0, the coefficient ideal aℤ+((-b+√D)/2)ℤ is the positive rational multiple a·(wℤ+ℤ), hence has the same narrow class. Keep the oriented sign clause when a<0. Export the remaining DIT coefficient actions (2.3)–(2.5) using the supplier dictionary. For every primitive Q representing A and each genus factor δ, provide a positive represented m coprime to δ and a nonzero integral ideal B=(α)𝔞⁻¹ of absolute norm m in A⁻¹, including integrality and proper-basis compatibility. No form reduction, composition, binary carrier or content theory is rebuilt here.

sourceIssues.printed: The paragraph identifies χ(J) with both factor signs in D=d′d without restricting the displayed equality to positive D.
sourceIssues.correction: Qualify this sentence by D=d′d>0. For D<0 the factor signs are opposite, and in an imaginary field the distinguished principal class is trivial, so χ(J)=1. The real quadratic formula used in this roadmap is valid.
sourceIssues.reason: The section explicitly treats both signatures immediately before and after this paragraph. Take D=−4=1·(−4): the two displayed factor signs are 1 and −1, so the asserted equality cannot hold without the real restriction. In an imaginary quadratic field every nonzero norm is positive, hence narrow and ordinary ideal equivalence coincide. This is a missing local qualifier, not a counterexample to (7.8), which already splits the real sign cases.

checked.note: The baseline kernel-range and principal-class dichotomy imply the exact pair, including J=1; first isomorphism gives the quotient.
Quotient lifting gives existence precisely on the kernel condition; surjectivity gives uniqueness. The ℤˣ target is a homomorphism target, not an arbitrary function.
The existing additive/square quotient equivalence, fibre equivalence, finite narrow group and ramified-prime two-rank give the stated cardinality and equal nonempty fibres.
The pinned singleton evaluation and product decomposition give the subset formula; D>0 gives equal complementary signs. Source issue E1 independently confirmed.
The signed odd-prime factors detect residue 3; full-product positivity forces the sole possible even factor to be positive. Empty product and D<0 boundary checked.
The pinned valuation criterion specializes because every odd divisor of a fundamental positive discriminant has valuation one. D=1 allowed; 9 is an explicit nonfundamental counterexample.
The pinned J-square criterion plus the two arithmetic adapters gives both equivalences. Principal-genus and character product APIs give all-even/descent consequences, without claiming J=1.
The prime divisor forces J nonsquare and hence nontrivial; the exact kernel, norm-unit equivalence and class-number/kernel identity give every conclusion. No converse claimed.

The conditional positive-representation/norm-ideal proof is sound and uses no comparison conclusion as input.
